newsitem.title: UK: Analysts call for greater transparency on LME.
newsitem.headline: Analysts call for greater transparency on LME.

text.p: Mining analysts wanted greater transparency on the London Metal Exchange (LME) to result from the Securities and Investments Board's (SIB) review of the metal markets currently underway.
In a question-and-answer session at the end of the LME metals seminar on Monday, a panel of analysts agreed the lack of transparency was a top priority.
"(LME brokerage firm) Brandeis would like to see more transparency in terms of the over-the-counter (OTC) market and a more formal reporting system," said Robin Bhar of Brandeis.
"On a personal note I would also like to see a wider representation on the LME's board (of directors)," he added.
"I would like to see a similar breakdown of open interest that COMEX gives now," said Malcolm Southwood of J B Were & Son.
"The LME needs greater transparency, possibly through large position reporting," said Claire Hassal of Brook Hunt and Associates.
One analysts said the LME should strive to bring more of its users under the membership umbrella.
"We should look to bring consumers and companies like Sumitomo within the membership fold," said Tariq Salaria of Metal Bulletin Research.
The LME did not know the extent of Sumitomo Corp's loss-making copper positions because a large part of that position was not in LME contracts, LME chief executive David King said earlier on Monday.
"There was a huge amount of OTC business and physical business about which we knew absolutely nothing," he said.
